content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define excretion and explain why it is necessary
Identify the main excretory products and organs
Understand the importance of removing waste products

is the removal of metabolic waste products from the body. These wastes are produced by chemical reactions inside cells and must be removed because they are toxic if they accumulate. Excretion is essential for maintaining a stable internal environment.
The removal of metabolic waste products and excess substances from the body
Waste products are made inside cells
They would be toxic if allowed to build up
Faeces are NOT excretory products - the material was never inside cells!
Dissolves in blood forming carbonic acid
Urea is toxic in high concentrations
Removal of amino group from amino acids
Excess amino acids cannot be stored
Remainder used for respiration or converted to fat
Small amounts of urea, water, salts (sweat)
CO₂ produced by respiration in cells
Sweating is primarily for temperature regulation, not excretion
Sweating is mainly for temperature regulation
We only excrete when we go to the toilet
We excrete CO₂ with every breath
All carbon dioxide comes from the lungs
CO₂ is produced by all cells; lungs just excrete it
Substance produced by chemical reactions in cells
Removal of amino group from amino acids
Excretion removes metabolic waste products from the body
Main wastes: CO₂ (from respiration) and urea (from protein breakdown)
CO₂ excreted by lungs; urea by kidneys
Urea made in liver from excess amino acids (deamination)
Excretion essential to prevent toxic build-up
Also involves removing excess water and salts
